cases.name: N1_i_z13_transposition
cases.intended: P2 with the entries at columns 2 and 9 of row 4 (a = 7) swapped. For linear rows r, j the swap removes the differences (a_r-a_j)c1, (a_r-a_j)c2 and adds a_r*c2-a_j*c1, a_r*c1-a_j*c2; the difference row stays a permutation iff these sets coincide, i.e. iff a_r(c2-c1) = 0 or a_j(c2-c1) = 0 mod 13, i.e. iff a_r = 0 or a_j = 0. With a_4 = 7 exactly the row pairs (4,j) with a_j != 0 fail: (0,4),(2,4),(3,4),(4,5),(4,6); (1,4) survives (row 1 is the zero row). Bridge: (0,4) -> all 13 columns of L_4 not Latin (its rows stay Latin); (2,4),(3,4),(4,5),(4,6) -> those square pairs not orthogonal; L_1 stays orthogonal to L_4

cases.name: N2a_ii_z13_dup_row0
cases.intended: P2 with row 6 replaced by a copy of row 0 (a = 5): row pair (0,6) has all 13 differences 0; every other pair keeps a non-zero multiplier difference (5 - a_s for a_s in 0,12,1,7,3). Bridge: L_6[c][g] = g, every column constant -> all 13 columns of L_6 not Latin (rows Latin); no orthogonality failure, since L_6 is still orthogonal to L_1..L_5 in the distinct-pairs sense

cases.name: N3_iii_z9_k4
cases.intended: Z_9, k = 4, rows 0, x, 2x, 4x. Multiplier differences: 1, 2, 4 against row 0, 1 for rows (1,2), 3 for rows (1,3), 2 for rows (2,3). The units of Z_9 are the residues prime to 3, so 2 is a unit (2*5 = 10 = 1 mod 9) and the only non-unit difference is 3: exactly row pair (1,3) fails (3x takes only the values 0, 3, 6). Bridge: L_1, L_2, L_3 have column multipliers 1, 2, 4 (units) -> all Latin; square pair (1,3) not orthogonal
